title: Split bookmark
idea: Shelf's bookmark cut once down its centre line, so the two halves stand as a pause sign. Each half keeps its half of the notch, and the eye closes the two slopes back into one bookmark; a pause and a bookmark both mean stop here and come back later.
built: geom.bookmark at 42 dp wide with today's proportions, drawn as one compound path of two pieces, centred on its drawn box (reach 32.0 of the 33 dp safe radius, centroid 1.9 dp above centre). The cut is 6.3 dp, 0.15 of the width. The app's own pause button (Lucide pause filled with the 1.75 stroke: bars 5.75 wide, gap 2.25) has a gap of 0.164 of its width; a hair narrower here lets the bookmark lead, and from 0.18 up the halves start to read as two separate bars. Each half runs from its tip up its half of the notch to the cut, so the slope is unbroken. The four corners the cut makes take the tip radius (1.5/34 of the width) and only the outer shoulders are round, so the halves read as one shape cut through.
small: Nothing is dropped at any size. 48 px: 28 x 34 px, 4 px cut, shoulders r 3, each notch edge from the tip at (10, 41) to the cut at (22, 33), a 2:3 slope close to the master's. 32 px: 20 x 24 px with a 4 px cut, since a 2 px cut went faint where this size shows at 16 CSS px on 2x screens; notch 5 over 8. 16 px: 10 x 12 px, 2 px cut, notch 3 over 4, shoulders r 1. I tried 1:2 slopes at 48 and 32: cleaner steps, but visibly flatter than the master's notch and no fewer grey pixels. Glyph: 16 x 20 px with a 2 px cut, the master's proportion, because phones draw it at 2.6 times or more.
risks: It reads as a pause sign, and as listening only to someone who already knows Shelf reads articles aloud; pause on its own says something is playing now. Out of context, most of all at 16 px, it can pass for a media app's pause button before it reads as a bookmark; the angled feet keep it Shelf's. Near lookalikes: a Roman numeral II, a parallel sign. The gap carries the whole idea, so every later redraw has to keep it open.
